title: Where the Line Goes
scopeNote: This keeps the continuum, the movable category line and the two competing rules, cut from six dimensions to the two that make the argument: trait extremity and interference. The other four dimensions, the profile builder and the worked pair stay in the longer version. Distress is deliberately not one of the two, for the reason the original gives.
summary: Four invented profiles on two dimensions, a line you can move and two rules that can draw it. Two profiles change sides when the rule changes, and neither of them moves.
learningObjectives: Explain why unusual traits are not sufficient for a disorder-level interpretation.
Distinguish trait extremity from interference and say why neither implies the other.
Explain what changes when a continuum is cut into a category.
Explain why the number of people above a line is set by where the line goes.
Recognise that a chosen boundary does not make what falls either side of it unreal.
Say why distress belongs to a separate question from interference.
interactionTypes: a judgement about what makes a pattern a clinical question
a live control over where the category line falls
a toggle between two rules that could draw it
four profiles that never move while their classification does
a fictional population share that follows the cut
a guided route showing the two profiles that change sides
privacy: Nothing is collected, stored or transmitted. The page contains no diagnostic instrument, returns no diagnosis, asks the reader nothing about themselves or anybody they know, names nobody, names no diagnosis and reproduces no criteria from any classification system.
dataStatus: Four invented profiles, each a pair of numbers on invented scales, chosen to occupy the four corners of the space. The population figure is an invented normal distribution used only to show that a count follows a cut, and is not an estimate of anything.
contentNote: The activity concerns the boundary between personality description and clinical interpretation. It affirms that personality difficulties are real and cause real suffering, and its subject is the step from a continuum to a category rather than any condition, person or classification system.
accessibilityNotes: Keyboard operable throughout. The line is a native range input reporting its value in text, and the rule is a button carrying aria-pressed with a visible word saying which rule is in force. Every profile's two numbers and its current side are in a real table with row and column headers, and the side is given in words, so the figure is never the only route to the classification. In the figure each marker is labelled with its side in words as well as being filled or hollow, both axes are named in words, and the description states the line, the rule, which profiles are above and that the markers do not move. Nothing is timed and there is no motion.
simulationNotes: Each profile is a pair of numbers on a 0 to 100 scale, and neither is computed from the other. That is the point of the design: a tool that derived interference from trait extremity would build in the assumption it exists to examine, which is that unusual traits and difficulty are the same thing. The four profiles occupy the four corners of the space, so that switching the rule moves exactly two of them across the line while none of them moves, and those two are the argument: unusual traits with little interference, and ordinary traits with a great deal of it. The population figure uses a fictional normal distribution on whichever dimension the current rule uses, and exists to show the second decision, that the share above the line changes by more than twentyfold across the range of the control while nobody in that population changes. Distress is deliberately absent. In the full version it is a dimension of its own and is excluded from the functioning composite, because it is a reason for help in its own right and can be present without interference or absent with it; folding it into either of these two axes would have hidden that, and the caution says so. The figure uses short profile labels because the full names overflow the drawing area and were being silently cut off; the table keeps the full wording. Simplifications, all stated: real assessment is not two numbers and a threshold but involves history, context, corroboration and time; a boundary being a decision does not make what falls either side of it unreal or make categories useless, and their practical value is stated; and the page takes no position on any particular classification system.
readmeTopic: what changes when a continuum is cut into a category, and who decides
